turns.question: Were any CSF studies performed during the age-75 admission, and if so, what were the cell count, protein, and any oligoclonal band or antibody results?

assessment.summary: A 75-year-old man has escalating left frontotemporal focal seizures (now daily) with worsening memory. MRI at 74 and 75 shows only mild diffuse atrophy without structural lesion, hippocampal sclerosis, or vascular pathology; FDG-PET shows no significant hypometabolism. EEG at 75 confirms left frontotemporal ictal onset with left hemispheric spread, while EEG at 74 showed right frontotemporal sharp waves, suggesting bilateral epileptogenic potential. Seizures recurred at 72 after remission on valproate, worsened despite gabapentin addition at 74. The high seizure burden is a plausible contributor to cognitive decline, but the bilateral epileptiform activity and progressive memory symptoms raise concern for an underlying inflammatory or autoimmune process not yet excluded. CSF findings are needed to assess for inflammation or autoimmunity.
